result:
I played all 24 months. All three training runs finished on time, and no inference demand went unserved.

**Final settlement: net cost $1,717.8M**, with no penalties.
- Total spent was $2,135.6M: GPU purchases $1,425M, power $234M, cloud contracts $596M, spot $0. Resale brought back $119.4M.
- GPUs still owned or in the queue at the end were valued at $584.2M, which lowers the net cost.
- Contract and power payments still owed after month 23 add $166.4M.

**Training runs**

| Months | Done / needed |
|---|---|
| 0–7 | 153 / 60 |
| 8–15 | 259 / 140 |
| 16–23 | 325 / 320 |

**How it played out**
- **Supply was tight for most of the game.** In month 0 the cloud providers only accepted 3 of the 5 kH I tried to reserve, which was the first sign. So I locked in three 24-month reservations early, at about $1.63–1.83M per kH-month. The contract price then climbed to about $3.5–4M.
- **Inference grew at the fast rate (about 7% a month).** Demand went from about 6 kH to about 30 kH, so the last window needed about 75 kH of capacity. I bought 33k gen H GPUs between months 0 and 9, before gen N launched. The vendor kept shipping them after gen H was discontinued.
- **Gen N launched in month 15.** The rumour of "around month 17" made a launch near 15 likely. When it was confirmed, I ordered 15k gen N GPUs and added three 6-month cloud reservations to cover the last window. It finished just 5 kH-months over its 320 target, with nothing spent on spot.
- **I sold surplus GPUs in months 22–23.** Once the last run was effectively done, I sold 6k gen H and 3k gen N, which brings in slightly more than their end-of-game valuation would.

**Where I lost money:** the first two windows finished far over target (153 vs 60, and 259 vs 140). Compute only counts in its own window, so roughly 210 kH-months were wasted. That came from buying gen H early to protect the last window, but cutting back on the 12-month and 24-month reservations would have saved a good share of it.
